newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metal futures end mostly firmer.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metal futures end mostly firmer.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures settled mostly higher in thin trade on Tuesday, buoyed by the firmer spot prices, traders said.
Market players were generally on the sidelines amid uncertainty over Russian President Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery and ahead of U.S. elections later on Tuesday.
Gold prices ranged from four yen per gram lower to seven yen firmer, with benchmark October finishing six yen up at 1,369 yen.
Spot gold was quoted at $378.80/379.10 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $378.60/379.00 in New York on Monday.

Traders said bearish sentiment in the bullion market remained intact. "Gold is unlikely to be lifted significantly until U.S. stocks start to go into a correctional phase. But support at around $377.5 could be maintained in the near term due to physical buying in Asia," one trader said.
Traders said the key to the bullion market hinges on whether the United States will raise its interest rates or leave them unchanged after the election.
Uncertainty over Yeltsin's health provided moderate psychological support to platinum futures, traders said.

Private investors bought a moderate amount of platinum futures, while trade houses bought spot platinum in arbitrage trade. Platinum futures ranged from five yen to eight yen per gram higher. Benchmark October was seven yen up at 1,384 yen.
Spot platinum was quoted at $381.25/382.00 per ounce at the Tokyo close, after opening at $381.00/381.75.
Activity in silver and palladium was sluggish.
Benchmark October palladium was down one yen at 426 yen.
Benchmark October silver was 1.1 yen per 10 grams firmer at 179.5 yen. -- Tokyo Commodity Desk +81-3-3432-7431
